properties.areaDesc: Transylvania, NC
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 11:25PM EDT until October 11 at 2:15AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southwestern Transylvania County in western North
Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 215 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots. Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible. A
few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible. A small
culvert washout or two is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1125 PM EDT, Light to moderate showers are moving from south
to north across the county, with heavier showers approaching from
the south. Rainfall of 2 to 4 inches have fallen over the past 12
hours. The rainfall has accumulated steadily, allowing soils to
slowly saturate and runoff to slowly increase.

Out of bank conditions will develop by area streams such as
Little River, Davidson River, and Forks of the Upper French Broad
River.

Additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms are expected to
develop over the next few hours and the threat will persist
through the early morning hours on Sunday. These showers and
storms will be very efficient at producing heavy rainfall. Soils
are saturated and streams are swollen. Therefore, additional
heavy rain may quickly create new areas of flooding and cause
previous areas of flooding to redevelop.  As a result, Flash
Flood Warnings may be issued tonight. Caution is advised near any
stream or other vulnerable area. Seek higher ground immediately
if heavy rain develops. Please have a plan in place should flash
flooding develop and do not hesitate to act. Please heed all
evacuation orders from Emergency Management officials.

stream or other vulnerable area. Seek higher ground immediately
if heavy rain develops. Please have a plan in place should flash
flooding develop and do not hesitate to act. Please heed all
evacuation orders from Emergency Management officials.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Lake Toxaway, Gorges State Park, B.R. Parkway-Black Balsam To
Mount Pisgah, Balsam Grove and Sapphire.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Only when it is safe to do so, please report flooding or landslides
threatening roads or property to the National Weather Service
Greenville-Spartanburg by calling 1...800...2 6 7...8 1 0 1, by
posting on our Facebook page, or by posting on X using hashtag
NWSGSP. Your message should describe the specific location, address,
or intersection where impacts occurred and the depth of flooding
observed.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in North
Carolina...

French Broad River at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W Fletcher affecting
Buncombe and Henderson Counties.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...French Broad River near at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W
Fletcher.

* WHEN...Until Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, Action Stage continues.  Glenn Bridge Park
river access is experiencing minor flooding.  Westfeldt Park is
experiencing scattered flooding.  French Broad River floodwaters
are causing isolated to widely scattered farmland flooding.

At 13.0 feet, Minor Flood Stage.  French Broad River floodwaters are
now inundating Banner Farm Rd.  Floodwaters may be approaching
portions of Glenn Bridge Rd.  Farmland and other low-lying areas
within the French Broad River Valley from Etowah to Avery Creek are
experiencing scattered flooding.  Glenn Bridge Park and river access
is experiencing scattered flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 PM EDT Saturday the stage was 9.3 feet and rising.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 12.5 feet
tomorrow morning.
- Action/Advisory Stage is 10.0 feet.
- Minor Flood Stage is 13.0 feet.
properties.instruction:

alternative route.

flood impacts, flood history, FEMA Flood Hazard Layers, and more,

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 10 at 11:16PM EDT until October 11 at 5:15AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Henderson County in western North Carolina...
Polk County in western North Carolina...
Eastern Transylvania County in western North Carolina...

* Until 515 AM EDT.

* At 1116 PM EDT, Earlier today, a prolonged period of steady
rainfall produced 3-6 inches across eastern Transylvania,
Henderson, and Polk counties, saturating area soils and causing
scattered areas of nuisance flooding.  Doppler radar shows several
rounds of torrential rainfall has moved through the area from the
south, capable of producing 2-3 inches of rainfall on top of
saturated soils.  This rainfall will exacerbate areas of ongoing
nuisance flooding and cause new areas of Minor flooding to develop.

* Areas of greatest concern include along the Little River from Cedar
Mountain to Penrose; the Davidson River near Pisgah Forest; the
French Broad River from Brevard to Mills River; Mud Creek from Crab
Creek to Hendersonville to Mountain Home; White Oak Creek from Mill
Spring to Green Creek; and Boylston Creek near Forge Mountain.

* Additional areas of Minor Flooding are expected to develop over the
next 1-3 hours.  Please obey all barricades and heed all evacuation
orders from local Emergency Management officials.  Only a few
inches of water can strand your vehicle and only 6 inches of water
can sweep your vehicle away.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect flash flooding of low-lying areas near streams,
including parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat- access
areas, and campgrounds.  Significant flooding of
poor-drainage areas are likely, impacting travel.
Low-lying roadways are likely to be flooded, requiring
barricades.   An isolated landslide or two cannot be ruled
out.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Hendersonville, Brevard, Columbus, Mills River, Fletcher, Flat
Rock, Etowah, Mountain Home, Laurel Park and Tryon.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

The additional heavy rain will increase the risk of landslides and
debris flows, especially in areas where landslides have occurred in
the past. Be especially alert if you live near a stream, particularly
at the base of a mountain or in a cove. Watch for signs that a
landslide may be imminent, including loose-moving soil and rocks or a
sudden increase in streamflow. Stay indoors and do NOT go outside to
investigate. Escape vertically inside your home by moving upstairs or
getting on top of counters to avoid being swept away.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; San Diego County Inland Valleys; San Diego County Mountains; San Diego County Deserts
properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued October 10 at 8:11PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
HLSSGX

This product covers EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA

**Impacts from Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel Expected in San Diego
County Late Tonight through Early Sunday Afternoon**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for San Diego County
Coastal Areas, San Diego County Deserts, San Diego County
Mountains, and San Diego County Valleys

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 240 miles south-southeast of San Mateo Point CA or about
180 miles south-southeast of Mouth of Tijuana River CA
- 30.0N 116.5W
- Storm Intensity 60 mph
- Movement North-northeast or 15 degrees at 36 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Impacts from Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel Expected in San Diego County
Late Tonight through Early Sunday Afternoon.

Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel is currently about 190 miles south of San
Diego, moving north-northeast towards Northern Baja at about 36 mph.
Rachel is expected to make landfall south of the US/Mexico Border
tonight. Though Rachel no longer has tropical characteristics,
tropical storm level impacts will likely affect San Diego County. A
Tropical Storm Watch remains in effect for all of San Diego County.
The main concerns with Tropical Storm Rachel are coastal flooding,
wind, and periods of heavy rain which could lead to localized flooding
and flash flooding. The majority of impacts from the tropical storm
are expected late tonight through early Sunday afternoon.

South swell from Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel will arrive on Sunday.
The combination of south and northwest swells, increased onshore
winds, and high tides over 7 feet will maintain a threat of coastal
flooding and beach erosion along area beaches. Surf on Sunday is
currently expected to peak at 6 to 9 feet, decreasing to 3 to 6 feet
for Monday and Tuesday. Confidence in impactful coastal flooding is
high, with significant coastal flooding and beach erosion likely.

Widespread rain is expected late tonight into late Sunday morning from
Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel. There is expected to be a gradient in
rainfall amounts with the higher amounts over San Diego County, the
mountains, and parts of the low desert. Peak rainfall rates of 0.50 to
0.60 inches are possible for the coast and valleys, 0.50 to
0.70 inches per hour possible for the deserts, and 0.70 to 1 inch per
hour for the mountains. Current forecast has rainfall totals of
0.50 to 1.25 inches for the coast, valleys, and deserts and 1 to
2.5 inches for the mountains. Areas of flash and urban flooding are
probable, especially where the maximum rainfall rates occur. The San
Diego River at Fashion Valley is currently forecast to crest at
8.1 feet (action/monitor stage) just before noon on Sunday. Those with
interests near the San Diego River should continue to monitor the
forecast.

Increased winds are expected with the onset and passage of
Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel. Sustained winds of 39+ mph are expected
on the southeast side of the storm. Based on the current track, more
southern and eastern parts of San Diego County are most likely to see
winds of this magnitude. Regardless, strong sustained winds and wind
gusts can be expected on Sunday. Winds will likely be enhanced by
local terrain with gusts 40 to 55 mph on the desert slopes of the
mountains and into the deserts. Local gusts up to 60 mph possible on
mountain ridges and in passes and canyons. Winds are expected to
remain elevated in Rachel's wake with continued strong gusts on the
desert mountain slopes into the deserts through Monday morning.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Prepare for hazardous wind having possible limited impacts across
EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA. Potential impacts in this area
include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted, especially in coastal and valley locations that
don't typically experience strong winds. Some fences and
roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA, little to no impact
is anticipated.


* FLOODING RAIN:
Prepare for life-threatening rainfall flooding having possible
extensive impacts across San Diego County. Potential impacts include:
- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in
multiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, arroyos, and
ditches may become dangerous rivers. In mountain areas,
destructive runoff may run quickly down valleys while
increasing susceptibility to rockslides and mudslides. Flood
control systems and barriers may become stressed.
- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed
away. Many places where flood waters may cover escape routes.
Streets and parking lots become rivers of moving water with
underpasses submerged. Driving conditions become dangerous.
Many road and bridge closures with some weakened or washed out.

Prepare for dangerous rainfall flooding having possible significant
impacts across San Diego County.

* OTHER COASTAL HAZARDS:
- High tides over 7 ft, combined with high surf and gusty onshore
winds will increase the threat for coastal flooding across area
beaches. Additionally surf of 6 to 9 ft will create dangerous swimming
conditions. Significant coastal flooding and beach erosion is
likely.


PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
If you live in a place particularly vulnerable to flooding, such as
near the ocean, in a low-lying or poor drainage area, in a valley, or
near a river, plan to move to safe shelter on higher ground.

Always heed the advice of local officials and comply with orders that
are issued. Do not needlessly jeopardize your life or the lives of
others.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather Radio and local news
outlets for official storm information. Listen for possible changes
to the forecast.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in San Diego CA around 2 AM PDT, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

Impacts from Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel Expected in San Diego
County Late Tonight through Early Sunday Afternoon
